questions: What happens if multiple indices have the same maximum value when choosing which index to decrement?
Does the game end immediately when S becomes {1,2,...,N}, or after the current player's turn completes?
What is the exact condition for "A_i" in the operation description - is it just that A_i > 0?
How are ties broken when both players have equally good moves available?
Is the initial state guaranteed to have at least one index i where A_i > 0?
What happens if N = 0 - is this case excluded by the constraints?
Does "play optimally to win" mean each player tries to maximize their own winning probability?
Are there any restrictions on which index i can be chosen beyond A_i > 0 and 1 ≤ i ≤ N?
answers: There's no 'maximum value' requirement; any index i with A_i ≥ 1 may be freely chosen.
The game ends immediately upon the operation that makes S = {1,...,N}; that player wins.
The condition is 1 ≤ A_i; a player may choose i only if A_i is currently positive.
Not applicable; optimal play determines the outcome deterministically, no tie-breaking is needed.
Yes, since A is given as a sequence of positive integers, all A_i > 0 initially.
Not applicable; N is guaranteed to be at least 1.
Both players play deterministically to guarantee a win whenever one is achievable for them.
No further restriction beyond A_i ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ i ≤ N.
inline_prompts: Fennec and Snuke are playing a board game. You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of positive integers of length N. Also, there is a set S, which is initially empty. Fennec and Snuke take turns performing the following operation in order, starting with Fennec. - Choose an index i such that A_i ≥ 1. Subtract 1 from A_i, and if i\notin S, add i to S. - If S=\lbrace 1,2,\dots,N \rbrace, the game ends and the player who performed the last operation wins. Note that it can be proven that until a winner is determined and the game ends, players can always make a move (there exists some i such that 1\leq A_i). Both Fennec and Snuke play optimally to win. Determine who will win. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print Fennec if Fennec wins, or Snuke if Snuke wins. The judge is case-insensitive; for example, if the correct answer is Fennec, outputs such as fennec, FENNEC, or fEnNeC will also be accepted. Constraints - 1\leq N\leq 2\times 10^5 - 1\leq A_i\leq 10^9 (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
